 Tihar has seen escapes since 1965: How Delhi’s prisons are trying to keep inmates from breaking out

 Abhay / TNN / Oct 29, 2026, 12:37 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium

 Print Recent Jailbreaks Expose Prison Security Gaps in Delhi, TN (AI image) The great escape
 The daring jailbreak by 17 undertrials from Thekkam patti prison in Tamil Nadu's Theni district this week has brought prison security into focus. In Delhi, jail officials maintain that security measures across the capital’s three prison complexes are already stringent, with multiple layers of security and surveillance in place. TOI’s Abhay takes a closer look at the arrangements and the lessons from past jailbreaks Delhi's three prisons can house over 20K inmates
 Tihar 14,500 Rohini 2,000 (approx) Mandoli 4,000+ From Sobhraj to Phoolan’s killer, Tihar no stranger to jailbreaks
 2015 Two inmates fled. One was held, while the other managed to escape but was caught later 2013 A prisoner died after falling from a moving truck while trying to escape from inside the prison 2011 Two undertrial drug addicts made a dash for Gate No. 3 along with eight other inmates while being transported in a van. They escaped but were caught 2004 MP Phoolan Devi’s killer, Sher Singh Rana, escaped from prison after getting his aide to pose as a cop. His friend, Sandeep Thakur, came to the jail disguised as a policeman to take him for his trial hearing 1986 Charles Sobhraj, lodged in Tihar for allegedly committing 20 murders, escaped after drugging security guards on his birthday 1983 Several students, arrested for arson and rioting, escaped from Tihar by exploiting its visitor identification system. Visitors bore stamps on their wrists, which the students transferred onto their own wrists in the May heat. Jail authorities failed to notice that three times as many visitors left as had entered 1976 Thirteen prisoners escaped by digging a tunnel near the prison's wall 1965 The first person to make an unauthorised exit from Tihar was an American smuggler, Daniel Walcott What expert says
 Sunil Kumar Gupta, former spokesperson and legal advisor to Tihar Jail, offered insights into the reasons behind several prison escapes: Reasons behind escapes
 Gupta explained that, in one case, inmates wanted to meet their families. In the 2015 escape, the two inmates reportedly wanted to break free from the restrictions of prison life and live without its rules and constraints In his book, Gupta also discusses two other prison escapes, one in 1981 and another in 2004. In the 1981 incident, an inmate escaped on the pretext of receiving medical treatment. In the 2004 incident, an escaped inmate reportedly asked a jail official for directions to a bus stop while outside the prison What prisons are doing to strengthen security
 Extensive security deployment
 More than 5,000 personnel, including prison staff and external security forces, are deployed across Delhi’s three prison complexes Four-layer security system
 Security is organised into four layers: prison staff in the first, Tamil Nadu Special Police (TSP) in the second, Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) in the third and Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in the fourth Defined responsibilities
 Tihar Jail staff manage internal prison operations; TSP personnel guard watchtowers and high-security areas; ITBP personnel handle day-to-day patrolling; and CRPF personnel guard the gates Extensive CCTV surveillance
 More than 7,000 cameras are installed across the three prison complexes, with dedicated rooms for monitoring the footage Regular security assessments
 Routine inspections and day-to-day security assessments are conducted to identify and address potential vulnerabilities Mobile jammers
 Tihar and Mandoli prison complexes have large-scale mobile signal jammers, while Rohini Jail also has jamming systems to restrict unauthorised mobile phone use Cell searches and surprise inspections
 Prison authorities conduct thorough cell searches and unannounced checks to detect prohibited items and prevent security breaches Security during prisoner movement
 Delhi Armed Police personnel escort inmates when they are taken outside prison premises Restricted access for maintenance work
 Inmates are not permitted to clean sewers. Instead, the relevant agency is called in to carry out the work. Its personnel are subject to security checks and are required to enter and exit through a designated gate Routine staff transfers
 Prison staff are periodically transferred to prevent them from developing overly close relationships with inmates and to reduce the risk of collusion Deployment of Tamil Nadu Special Police (TSP)
 The deployment at Tihar began in Aug 1980, following security concerns raised by the 1976 jailbreak. The rationale was to bring in personnel from another state to reduce the risk of local connections and potential collusion between prisoners and prison staff
